you enjoy distinct character playstyles and builds
you like straightforward controls and deep challenge

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players note that attacks happen automatically while movement requires manual control.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having automatic attacks where the character only moves during matches without manual aiming or shooting controls.

citations.review_text:
Extremely boring game. Firstly the game lacks style. The UI looks soulless and is honestly a text ridden eye sore. The art style was nice but I wish they did more of it like incorporating into the UI design.

The gameplay loop is boring. Your attacks are automatic so all you do is select upgrades and run around and most likely get cornered (although that may be a skill issue lol)

The sound design was quite boring. The music felt bland and the sound design made the game struggle in a way. Because your game is mainly automatic you still want the players to have a sense of achieving something. The sound effects lack power and the satisfaction of killing something. So it makes the playthrough feel less of a fast pace route like and more something along the lines of cookie clicker.

 I never really write negative reviews but I feel quite strongly about my opinions on this game and I want to share my criticisms for this actually good roguelike idea (although I am pretty harsh lol)

Anyways 5-6/10

It is a good game, but I wasn't looking for something so simple. I didn't love that my character can only move during the match and nothing else, like pointing or shooting in some direction. The most interesting part of the game is in between rounds where you can pick different objects to change the outcome.

I was looking for something more complex, but I guess there will be people that enjoy it.

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players praise the distinct character builds, lightweight performance, and accessible yet challenging gameplay.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that individual characters have completely distinct playstyles and offer varied builds and weapon choices.

citations.review_text:
I dont know why it took me so long to play this game. One of the things I love most about Brotato is its ease of entry. The game's intuitive controls and straightforward gameplay make it accessible to players of all skill levels, allowing you to jump in and start playing right away.

But what really sets Brotato apart is its level of customization. With a wide range of options available, from character builds to weapon choices, I found myself experimenting with different combinations to see what worked best for me. The ability to try out new builds and strategies keeps the game feeling fresh and exciting, even after multiple playthroughs.

Speaking of which, the range of weapons in "Brotato" is incredible. From swords and daggers to ballistic options like pistols, shotguns and miniguns, there's always something new to try. Overall Brotato is a deliciously addictive game.

Really like the character choices that meaningfully mix up runs and make you think. Normally I tend to stick to one character and just get decent at using them, but here I want to try out more potatoes to see how it might mix up the run.

Experimenting with the different stats and such is pretty cool too. And I really like the upgrade system of combining to upgrade.

Brotato spuds. One of the most fun roguelites I’ve played. The potato theme could’ve been a gimmick, but it’s baked into the charm of the game. Every weird little spud character feels distinct and pushes you toward different builds, weapon combos, and synergies. One run you’re a speedy glass-cannon potato slicing aliens into au gratin, the next you’re an unkillable mashed tank going full hasselback with six flamethrowers. Maybe next you’re a big old pig of a spud, just windmilling around the arena.

The gameplay loop is crisp, chaotic, and very replayable. Unlocking new taters and experimenting with builds keeps things farm fresh. Highly recommended for all roguelite fans and, of course, potato enthusiasts. A must-play if you like potatoes and roguelites. Peak tuber gaming.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Mid-tier players enjoy short run lengths and variety, though they note the lack of story and multiplayer connection issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features local and couch co-op support for playing with friends or family.

citations.review_text: Brotato is a great game that I highly recommend. It has a lot of different characters that play very differently. Some give a unique spin on normal gameplay, but there are some that force you to play in a completely unique way to that class in order to succeed. I really enjoy the couch Co-Op for this game despite me not even knowing that was a feature. The DLC adds a lot of new characters and items most of which being really cool. I would recommend purchasing this if you enjoy the base game.

A very fun little game with a lot of replayability thanks to the huge variety of characters, each with their own playstyle. The short runs are great when you don't have much time, while still being interesting and satisfying. Even better with local co-op.

100% steam achievements
Time : 54.9H
Completion Difficulty : 2/10
Playthroughs : Many short run
Missables : None
DLC Required : Yes
Notable requirements : One run with each characters and at each difficulty

Couch co-op is thankfully alive and well. This is one of the most fun games to play with friends, although it's quite enjoyable in single-player, too. At around 100 hours in, I've finally completed the game. There's some luck required to beat the nightmare difficulty, given the nature of a roguelike, but the game overall is fairly forgiving.

I've somehow played this more than Vampire Survivors.  It's been fun figuring out how to unlock each character, and then trying to get each into the next danger level.  Levels are short and sweet, runs even out to level 20 are but 10-12 minutes long usually.  Very good for bite sized fun, and I've still hit the century mark in hours playing the game.  So, yeah...tis good.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Veterans highlight local multiplayer support, but find the highest difficulty levels overly punishing and dependent on luck.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the new nightmare difficulty as overly punishing, frustrating, and heavily dependent on luck rather than skill.

citations.review_text: I used to really love this game, but the new content sucks the life out of the old. D5 was a good max difficulty that required a good mix of skill and luck, and I beat every character on it on both maps twice. Nightmare mode is genuinely unplayable slop.
Кто балансил nightmare ты чё говна поел, на некоторых персах игра превращается чисто в казино в надежде что магазин нароллится нормальный

The nightmare mode makes you rely on luck way too much. Without good item rolls you just can't make it past wave 18 with some tatos (or even 14 if you are extremely unlucky). This is the most lame game design you can possibly think of: no skill decides if you win or not - just pure luck.

I've "perfected" this game on three different occasions because every time they release an update there are new achievements.  Neat! I get to play a game I enjoy.

Except now, whoever is a sadist on the dev team, please fire them.  This new nightmare mode is absolutely infuriating.  The game is no longer fun.  At least on danger 5 I had fun.  Nightmare is just; what the ♥♥♥♥. I actually have to uninstall this so I don't yeet my steam deck across the room.

It was pure fun until the last update No Pain No Gain, or more like No Fun All Pain. What's the point of introducing mechanics that make the game entirely RNG-based outside of meta builds? If that's the way this game is heading I think it's gonna die like many frustrating bullet hells. That's it, I said it - Brotato has become a bullet hell, which it was not before and that was the reason why it was so fun to play. At this point, if you want to try this game just reckon with the fact, that at some point gameplay becomes idiotic and frustatring beyond the point of tolerance.

Stupid update. The new developers really want to make people suffer (all pain no gain update). They didn't have any new ideas but really wanted to undermine the armor+dodge mechanic in this game. So they decided that throwing 100s of projectiles at the player that do billion damage each was the only thing missing in the game. All this does is make shop rng much more important and people can't have fun playing the non-strong potatoes. 

Not every game has to be a souls game, let us have our relaxed time. If you don't have any new ideas, stop updating the game.

TL;DR: I say this as someone who has cleared nightmare with multiple potatoes. The new update sucks. The developers don't understand what made this game fun.

After the last update, "Nightmare mode" completely ruined what made Brotato fun for me. The game used to feel challenging but fair — now it just feels overtuned and frustrating for the sake of difficulty.

Enemy scaling is absurd, elites become damage sponges, and half the runs feel RNG-dependent instead of skill-based. A lot of builds that were viable before are now useless unless you abuse a tiny handful of meta weapons/items. It went from a chaotic roguelike where experimentation was rewarding to “play this exact build or lose.”

Performance also feels worse during later waves with all the extra effects and enemies on screen. Add in some questionable balance changes and it honestly feels like the update was never properly tested.

Nightmare mode should be hard, not exhausting. Right now it feels more annoying than fun.

Trash game 2/10... Hope the next update will not be this bad, like this one.

The "All pain no gain" update made the game far less fun. The new difficulty puts way too much emphasis on getting the perfect spread of stats and economy, killing the viability of many items and runs. "Hard" can be fun, but this new "Danger 6" is just frustration.

Just beat the game and wanted to give my honest thoughts on it. First I'm going to straight up say that I enjoyed it throughout; Brotato is a wonderful example of the "pick up and play" concept, especially on a Steam Deck. It has an addicting, tight gameplay loop with lots of upgrades and quick waves. There is a large emphasis on shop purchases between rounds, ultimately affecting your builds in crazy & creative ways. [b][u]However, there are some flaws to consider before getting into it.[/u][/b]

Currently, much of the playerbase isn't too pleased with the "All Pain, No Gain" update, specifically a new difficulty setting. When playing on it, the game turns into a pretty exhausting and RNG-dependent experience. The scaling is extremely punishing; enemies are so overtuned that certain characters cannot win. It eliminates build variety and just isn't fun. I wish it were designed as a great challenge but one where you're rewarded for overcoming seemingly insurmountable odds.

My point is that the game is pivoting in a different direction, increasing the devs' workload for all the future balancing changes. It feels as if the formula we all love was unnecessarily tweaked, and a new precedent is being set where this behavior is seemingly ok. Hopefully that isn't the case.

Another gripe is the achievements, since this game does revolve around beating challenges. [i]Each update brings more of them.[/i] For any completionists out there, bear mind that a 100% requires clearing both the main and its DLC [b]twice[/b] with every character. A new, second DLC is coming out soon that will very likely increase said workload. Can definitely see why it might feel like a slog unlocking everything at later stages.

Despite these flaws, the game has lots of QoL accessibility features to tinker with: number of enemies, enemy HP & speed, turning off environmental projectiles, retrying waves after failure, etc. The punishing difficulty setting mentioned earlier is also completely optional …

citations.review_text:
A game about a potato. A potato that needs to survive because germs do not like potato. 

[b] I like the game and this is reason enough for me to recommend it. [/b] And played a lot. And even with friends on each their account. The most fun part is the multiplayer part. But it is only possible for one device to play with many. But how online? Remote Play is exactly this. The game gets streamed to other friends and they play on their device on specific this game. 

[b] What is fun? [/b]
The thousand combinations that are possible. And even support and compatibility for the mod community. 

And I have last words for the game devs. [b] You have my utmost respect. Thank you. [/b] It is still in active developement. You made a great game playable on literally on anything. Even on a potato computer.

Not for me ;) ;) ;)

(look @ hours played)

Nightmare mode a bit too much luck based. Very hard (a little bit too hard) to beat.
Other difficulties are challenging but just right.

Would love a co-op mode (not just the local one).
